### The Joy of Living in Jesus’s Shadow
Author: Marshall Segal
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/the-joy-of-living-in-jesuss-shadow
Passage: John 3:30
Points:
- People naturally wrestle with comparison and constantly strive for personal recognition.
- John the Baptist gladly stepped out of the spotlight to point everyone to Christ.
- The highest purpose of Christian life and ministry is funneling all glory to Jesus.
- True humility frees believers to rejoice when others succeed and flourish.
- Stepping into the Savior's shadow redirects our ambitions toward His exaltation.

### The Best Man
Author: Jill Briscoe
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-women/the-best-man-one-year-devotions-for-women-august-22.html
Passage: John 3:26
Points:
- Ministers and believers can easily be tempted by rivalry when others appear more successful.
- When John's followers worried about crowds leaving for Jesus, John refused to compete.
- Believers act only as the best man whose job is to honor the Bridegroom.
- We must welcome God giving honor and responsibilities to others as He sees fit.
- Living out the principle that Christ must increase brings genuine Christian joy.

### Christ Increasing
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/christ-increasing
Passage: John 3:29-30
Points:
- John rejected his disciples' view that Jesus was a rival seeking to eclipse their work.
- John understood that his God-given calling existed solely to direct attention to the Messiah.
- Like a friend of the bridegroom, John found full joy in seeing Christ take center stage.
- Scripture teaches that the path to true biblical honor begins with self-humbling before the Lord.
- Decreasing in personal prestige allows the greater glory of God to increase in us.

### Decreasing Into His Purpose
Author: Oswald Chambers
Site: My Utmost For His Highest
URL: https://utmost.org/classic/decreasing-into-his-purpose-classic/
Passage: John 3:30
Points:
- Spiritual workers must never make other people depend on them instead of God.
- Our primary duty is serving as friends of the Bridegroom who point souls directly to Christ.
- Human sympathy should never interfere with the Lord's work of convicting a heart.
- A servant of God experiences pure joy when a soul finally hears the Bridegroom's voice.
- Effective Christian service requires the worker to fade into the background so Jesus alone is seen.
